title: Private deploy GPU scaling playbook & estimator (Q1 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a compact, practical GPU fleet sizing + BOM estimator for Private/VPC deployments. It is intended for solution engineers and infra PMs to run quick scenario estimates, produce a first-pass hardware BOM, and verify operational constraints (power, racks, cooling, network).

Scope and assumptions (explicit):
- Workloads: text generation + chat with mixed short and long contexts (avg input+output tokens = 60). Also supports embedding workloads (treated separately).
- Target SLOs: 500ms p95 for single-turn gen, bursty traffic patterns allowed.
- Typical inference model variants: 7B quantized (q8_0), 13B quantized, and a 70B (sparsely used) model for high-quality paths.
- Node SKU options: 8x A40-class or 4x H100-80GB; the playbook uses H100-equivalent as baseline where noted.

Estimator quick formulas (operational):
- Requests per second (RPS) -> tokens per second (TPS): TPS = RPS * avg_tokens_per_request
- Tokens per second per GPU (sustained) depends on model and batching. Use reference table below.
- Required GPUs = ceil(TPS / tokens_per_second_per_gpu * safety_factor)
- Safety factor = 1.25 for baseline, 1.5 for high-availability/regional failover planning.

Reference performance (example numbers - bench your exact model):
- 7B q8_0: 25,000 tokens/s per H100-equivalent GPU
- 13B q8_0: 12,000 tokens/s per H100-equivalent GPU
- 70B (quantized but heavy): 2,500 tokens/s per H100-equivalent GPU

Power and rack budget rules of thumb:
- H100 node (4x H100): ~6.2 kW peak per 1U/2U server form factor design (varies by vendor).
- A40 8x node: ~4.2 kW peak.
- Leave 20% headroom in power and UPS for growth/real-world peaks.
- Cooling: estimate ~3.41 BTU per watt (so 6200 W -> ~21,142 BTU/hr).

Sample scenario: small SaaS customer (region: eu-west)
Inputs:
- RPS (steady average): 180
- Traffic mix: 70% 7B paths, 25% 13B, 5% 70B fallback
- Avg tokens per request: 60
- Safety factor: 1.25

Step 1 - compute TPS: TPS = 180 * 60 = 10,800 tokens/s
Step 2 - weighted tokens/s per model form (map rps to tokens):
- 7B fraction tokens/s = 0.70 * 10,800 = 7,560 TPS (handled by 7B GPUs)
- 13B fraction TPS = 0.25 * 10,800 = 2,700 TPS
- 70B fraction TPS = 0.05 * 10,800 = 540 TPS

Step 3 - GPUs required (using reference perf):
- 7B: GPUs = ceil(7,560 / 25,000 * 1.25) = ceil(0.378) = 1 GPU (H100-equivalent)
- 13B: GPUs = ceil(2,700 / 12,000 * 1.25) = ceil(0.28125) = 1 GPU
- 70B: GPUs = ceil(540 / 2,500 * 1.25) = ceil(0.27) = 1 GPU
Total GPUs (raw) = 3 GPUs -> round up to node units (if nodes are 4x GPUs, 1 node)

Practical pack rule: avoid 1 GPU per node inefficiency. For H100 nodes (4 GPU/node) we'd recommend packing to full nodes where possible. This scenario fits on 1 x 4-GPU node (reserve other slot for model variants or redundancy).

BOM line items (baseline estimate) for this scenario (EU datacenter, 1 node):
- Server: 1x 4-GPU H100-equivalent inference node (vendor model ABC-4H100)
- CPU: Dual-socket AMD Genoa 64-core (per vendor SKU)
- RAM: 1.5 TB DDR5 ECC
- NVMe: 8 TB NVMe for model cache + swap
- NICs: 2x 100Gbps (bonded)
- PDU/PDUs: 2x redundant PDUs per rack (shared across racks)
- Rack space: 1U/2U depending on vendor; provision 2U for node + 1U for management
- Network switch: Top-of-rack 32-port 100GbE (if stand-alone rack)
- Rack power: 10kVA provisioned (with 20% headroom)
- Optional: KMS HSM appliance (if customer requires on-prem key custody)

Cost quick math (vendor-quote ballpark):
- 4x H100 node: $420k list (varies widely) -> per-GPU $105k in this example
- Rack + networking + PDUs + cabling: $25k
- Installation & freight: $6k
- Support (3yr NBD): $45k
- One-time BOM total: ~496k USD (rounding)

Multi-region & HA considerations (sizing shortcuts):
- For two-region active-active: size each region for ~60-70% of expected peak and rely on cross-region failover for spikes; alternatively duplicate capacity for full redundancy (cost x2).
- For dedicated capacity with SLA 99.9% and canary/rollout capacity: add at least 1 extra node per region for canary/fallback.
- For warm standby (cold cache): reduce GPUs by 50% but account for model load time and cache priming window (minutes).

Operational checklist before procurement:
- Confirm rack U, per-rack power feed (A/B), UPS sizing and runtime expectations.
- Confirm datacenter cooling/cold-aisle containment and density limits (kW per rack) with colo.
- Validate vendor node dimensions, weight, and cable clearances for installation.
- Confirm network topology: BGP/peering for cross-region traffic, private links for control plane, dedicated VLANs for management.
- Confirm software license/agent compatibility (driver/kernel, RDMA/FSDPA, NCCL, CUDA/AMX stacks).

Example alternative cost-optimized layout (embedding-heavy, lower SLOs):
- Use 8x A40-class nodes (cheaper per node) with careful batching to hit similar throughput for non-latency-sensitive paths.
- Run smaller models at higher batching and push larger models to hosted fallback.

Sizing checklist + template fields for quick reuse (copy into a Google Sheet):
- Region, expected_peak_RPS, avg_tokens, p95_latency_ms_target, traffic_mix_7B_pct, traffic_mix_13B_pct, traffic_mix_70B_pct, tokens_per_sec_per_7B, tokens_per_sec_per_13B, tokens_per_sec_per_70B, safety_factor, rounding_policy (pack_nodes|pack_gpus)

Notes & caveats:
- Benchmark your actual model binary in the target node SKU. The reference numbers above are illustrative — we have seen >2x variance across frameworks, kernel versions, and quantization strategies.
- Embeddings have very different perf curves (embeddings TPS per GPU often lower per token but higher per request; treat separately).
- Licensing and customs (import taxes, lead times) can dominate time-to-first-response for on-prem BOMs — push procurement early.

Appendix A: quick-run estimator pseudo-steps for an engineer (copy into script):
1) read inputs (rps, avg tokens, model mix)
2) compute TPS = rps * avg tokens
3) split TPS by model fractions
4) for each model variant, GPUs = ceil((TPS_variant / perf_variant) * safety_factor)
5) total_gpus = sum(GPUs)
6) nodes = round_up_to_node_layout(total_gpus, gpus_per_node)
7) compute rack_count = ceil(node_u_total / u_per_rack)
8) compute power = sum(node_power) * 1.2 headroom
9) output BOM lines & rough costs

Appendix B: short troubleshooting notes from field runs:
- If p95 latency spikes under burst: check batching window and slow model fallbacks; reduce batching during spikes or enable LB token-based routing.
- If utilization is flat low (<30%): consider consolidating models onto fewer GPUs and offering lower-cost dedicated pools to customer.
- If OOMs appear during rollout: consider model sharding vs. quantization, increase host RAM, or use NVMe-backed cached KV stores.

Next steps / owners:
- Priya to convert this into a small Google sheet template with input fields and formula cells (by 2026-01-29).
- Ethan to run bench for 13B q8_0 on vendor X hardware and update perf numbers (due 2026-02-12).
- Maya to capture rack/power negotiation notes with colo ops for eu-west pilot (ongoing).

End of playbook.
